title: Quadratic Envelope Chirp with 2 Global Scalers (24 Layers)
scientific_hypothesis: Constraining the 24-layer chirp thickness profile to a quadratic envelope with only 2 global optimization parameters (chirp-rate scaler and chirp-amplitude scaler) plus localized perturbation noise will improve optimization convergence and achieve comparable or better dual-band performance than the 24-independent-variable approach, while reducing the risk of overfitting to specific wavelength points.
design_principle: Parameterize layer thicknesses using a symmetric quadratic envelope: layers 1-12 follow monotonic expansion from 50 nm to 85 nm, layers 13-24 follow monotonic contraction from 85 nm to 50 nm. The envelope shape is controlled by 2 global scalers, with small random perturbations (±5 nm) added to each layer to allow local optimization freedom.
proposed_topology: exactly 6 alternating HfO2/SiO2 pairs (12 finite layers)
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band
Maximize mean reflectance in 400-700 nm band
Minimize thickness variation between adjacent layers for manufacturability
manufacturing_considerations: Quadratic envelope ensures smooth thickness transitions
Perturbation bounds (±5 nm) reflect typical deposition tolerance
theory_basis: Evolutionary optimization with bounded variables reduces search space while maintaining solution quality
Graded index profiles reduce interface discontinuities compared to abrupt quarter-wave stacks
expected_advantages: Reduced optimization dimensionality improves convergence reliability
Quadratic envelope provides smooth thickness gradient for broadband visible rejection
Symmetric profile may improve angular tolerance
known_risks: Constrained parameterization may limit achievable performance compared to fully independent optimization
Quadratic envelope may not optimally separate the two target bands
execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer planar dielectric stack on Fused Silica substrate with Air incident medium. Layer sequence: alternating HfO2 (layers 1,3,5,...,23) and SiO2 (layers 2,4,6,...,24). Parameterize thicknesses using a symmetric quadratic envelope: layers 1-12 expand monotonically from 50 nm to 85 nm base profile, layers 13-24 contract monotonically from 85 nm to 50 nm base profile. Introduce 2 global optimization variables: chirp_rate_scaler (bounds 0.8-1.2) and chirp_amplitude_scaler (bounds 0.8-1.2) that scale the base envelope. Add per-layer perturbation noise bounded to ±5 nm. Optimize for maximum transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band and maximum reflectance in 400-700 nm band simultaneously. Use gradient-based or evolutionary optimizer with 100 iterations maximum. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates count, tightest_margin, and final thicknesses_nm array for all candidates. Topology realization override: disregard any symbolic repeat count, range, or ellipsis above and use exactly 6 alternating HfO2/SiO2 pairs (12 finite layers). Optimize only continuous physical thicknesses; the task compiler must fully expand every finite layer. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1530-1565 nm, 400-700 nm. soft objectives: High transmittance in 1530-1565 nm band; High reflectance in 400-700 nm band. behaviors to suppress or avoid: Low reflectance in 1530-1565 nm band; Low transmittance in 400-700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: Maximum 30 layers.
revision_reason: Implements feedback directive to replace 24 independent thickness variables with constrained quadratic envelope parameterization using 2 global scalers plus perturbation noise. Maintains 24-layer topology from route_02 while reducing optimization degrees of freedom.
